introduction.heading: Plumbing for West Valley homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in West Valley were built in 1985 or later, and about 42% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

West Valley City doesn't run its own water service. Most of the city is served by the Granger-Hunter Improvement District, which uses six deep wells for about a quarter of its supply and treated water from the Jordan Valley Water Conservancy District for the rest. The Kearns, Magna and Taylorsville-Bennion districts serve other parts of the city. Hardness averages about 176 mg/L (about 10 grains per gallon) across the Granger-Hunter service area, according to Granger-Hunter's 2026 water quality report, which covers 2025 testing. The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

Granger-Hunter is building treatment plants to remove naturally occurring manganese, iron and ammonia from its well water, which can turn water yellow or brown. The first plant is running and a second is under construction.
